new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Quote check: holds three overlapping Google Books feed snippets (id Se-BAAAAQBAJ, downloaded) whose union is exactly the quoted passage; the only differences are Google's snippet casing ("west of tunisia", "as verbs"). No page number is recoverable: Google Books HTML, Brill (not reachable by automated download) and the Leiden repository ("Toegang geblokkeerd / Access Blocked") all refuse this client; the only full copy online is an archive.org item that is explicitly a z-lib.org re-upload, so it was not used. Further feed queries (saved) surface no Figuig- or Sud-Oranais-specific stress remark in Kossmann 2013; the other 'accent' hit is "accent shift (Brugnatelli 1986)" in the number-morpho…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule is given for this language. The only statement that bears on it is family-level: in Northern Berber varieties west of Tunisia (which includes Figuig / Sud Oranais / Gourara) stress is non-phonemic and may not exist at all, so the author does not mark it. The language-specific descriptions opened (Boudot-Lamotte 1964 for Timimoun; Kossmann & Souag 2019 for the Sud Oranais) say nothing about accent placement; Boudot-Lamotte only notes that a few individual words (e.g. ïkzam 'grotte', u-hyert 'certes!') are 'toujours accentué(e)'.
new_statements.exceptions: Kossmann contrasts eastern Berber varieties, where stress is relevant and verbs shift stress by aspect; Boudot-Lamotte's remarks on always-accented words (initial vowel of ïkzam; the emphatic particle u-hyert; ultra-long accented a in ammen 'là-bas') are lexical/expressive notes, not exceptions to a rule.
new_statements.domain_note: Snippet-only, family-level remark by the author of the Figuig grammar; not a first-hand description of tazn1238 and not a placement statement. Confidence low; not catalog-grade.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog tazn1238 'Sud Oranais-Gourara' (ISO grr, alt. names Taznatit, Zenati, Shilha of Figuig) lumps three fieldwork traditions: Figuig (Morocco; Kossmann 1997/2014, Saa 2010, Benamara 2013), the Algerian Sud-Oranais ksour (Igli: Kossmann 2010; Asla/Boussemghoun/Tiout: El Idrissi 2017; Kossmann & Souag 2019), and Gourara/Timimoun taznatit (Boudot-Lamotte 1964, Ben Zaid 2016, Bellil, Mammeri). The only language-specific primary descriptions opened here are Timimoun (Boudot-Lamotte 1964) and the Sud-Oranais encyclopaedia entry; the quoted Kossmann 2013 remark is family-level (Northern Berber west of Tunisia), not variety-specific. WALS 'Berber (Figuig)' (bfg) maps to this glottocode.

sources.note: Gourara (Timimoun) taznatit. The 'caractéristiques phonétiques' paragraph (pp. 488-489) covers occlusion, palatalised dentals and r > h; no accent rule anywhere. Only ad-hoc glossary remarks that individual words are always accented (ïkzam 'grotte': 'La voyelle initiale du singulier (i) est toujours nettement accentuée'; u-hyert 'certes!': 'Mot toujours fortement accentué'; ammen 'là-bas' 'avec la voyelle a accentuée et ultra-longue').
